sentence: This project studies how thermal plasticity in plethodontid salamanders varies with reproductive condition across natural elevational gradients.
This project studies how gravity waves from weather near Earth's surface travel upward and disturb the ionosphere.
This project studies how the feathers of dinosaurs evolved into the wing that lets birds fly, using living birds and fossils.
This project builds methods that help robots learn to plan their movements in real time by using equations that describe motion.
This project studies how water quality and the living things in a river respond after a large sewage spill.
This project develops tools that predict how long marine energy turbines will keep working and designs those turbines together as one system.
This project studies how a mother's age affects the health of her offspring in the rotifer Brachionus manjavacas.
This project studies how to rebuild the geometry of a space from the areas of surfaces in equilibrium inside it.
This project tests an artificial intelligence platform that uses health records and CT scans to predict a person's risk of osteoporosis.
This project builds quantum computer methods that search for alloys made of multiple elements mixed in nearly equal amounts.
This project makes uneven tadpole particles and studies how their shape affects the way they move through a liquid crystal.
This project uses artificial intelligence and three-dimensional measurements of mammal teeth to study how the diets of mammals evolved.
This project builds tools that help scientists protect sensitive data and code in shared research workflows from attacks.
This project builds a flexible nail that forms inside the body during surgery to hold broken long bones in place.
This project explores evolutionary science through research on topics such as behavior, paleontology, genomics and how infectious disease evolves.
This project makes two dimensional materials with magnetic defects and studies whether those defects can serve as qubits for quantum computing.
This project replaces the camera and software on a transmission electron microscope so researchers can again view and record subcellular structures and nanoparticles.
